hints: Focus on what first ionisation energy really measures, removal of an electron from a single gaseous atom, not from a molecule.
Compare sulfur ($Z=16$) and chlorine ($Z=17$) in Period 3, they have the same inner shells but different nuclear charge.
Ask yourself which statements affect attraction of the nucleus for an outer electron, and which one is about $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{S}_8$ molecules instead.
walkthrough:
**Recall what first ionisation energy means**

Think of one separate gaseous atom losing its outer electron. It is an atomic property, not a molecular one.

$$\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^+(\text{g}) + \text{e}^-$$

**Compare S and Cl across Period 3**

Both have their outer electrons in n = 3, shielded by the same 1s, 2s and 2p inner electrons. So shielding is very similar.

Chlorine has 17 protons while sulfur has 16 protons, so chlorine has the higher nuclear charge pulling on a similar shell.

**Test each statement**

Statement 1 is true. More protons with similar shielding means greater effective nuclear charge and stronger attraction, so more energy is needed to remove the electron.

Statement 2 is false. Shielding does not increase significantly across the period because no new inner shell is added.

Statement 3 is false. Bond strength in $\text{Cl}_2$ or sulfur molecules is about covalent bond breaking, it has nothing to do with ionisation of separate atoms.

**Pick the combination**

Only statement 1 contributes. That matches the option for 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is correct, but 2 is wrong because shielding is almost the same across Period 3, and 3 is irrelevant because ionisation energy refers to gaseous atoms, not molecules.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 only are correct. While 1 is correct, 2 is a common trap. Chlorine does not have greater shielding, both S ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4$) and Cl ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5$) are shielded by the same 10 inner electrons.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 only are correct. Both are wrong. Shielding is similar, not greater, and molecular bond strength does not determine atomic ionisation energy.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is true. The increase from S to Cl is due to greater nuclear charge (17 protons vs 16 protons) acting on the same shell with similar shielding, giving a larger effective nuclear charge and a higher first ionisation energy.
